catalog_quote: Lawyer (2015, 2021) provides the only other analyses of Patwin phonetics and phonology. As with sister language Wintu (Pitkin 1984), stress assignment in Patwin is based on syllable weight (Lawyer 2021), where stress is associated with increased loudness, raised pitch, and vowel lengthening. Stressed vowels do not change in quality. In discussing Patwin intonation, Lawyer (2021) notes that phrases in the middle of a connected passage may end in rising pitch, whereas those uttered in isolation generally fall, regardless of whether they are questions or statements. Little other description of Patwin intonation currently exists. [Björklund 2024:2; line-break hyphen in 'vow-el' removed] ... • Patwin – again, stress on first or second syllable – seems to correlate fairly well with syllable weight [Buckley 2019, slide 56, immediately after the Wintu bullet 'two-syllable window – stress on second syllable if heavy, otherwise first'; slide 57: 'Wintun has first/second syllable stress – with important role for syllable weight – potentially germane to NE, though facts uncertain']

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress placement is predictable from syllable weight (as in Wintu, where stress falls on the second syllable if heavy, otherwise the first); the exact Patwin weight hierarchy is in Lawyer 2021 §3.4 'Stress Assignment and Syllable Weights' (pp. 66ff., Table 3.2 'Tentative syllable weight classes in Hill Patwin'), which was not accessible. Buckley's held handout paraphrases the same source as stress on the first or second syllable correlating with weight.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the open sources.
new_statements.exceptions: Older first-hand note, Kroeber 1932 p. 256 (saved file): 'Accent has not been written when it falls on the penult'; fn. 21 p. 260: 'Suffixes like -dihi, -sel, do not disturb the accent, which remains, unless written otherwise, on the penult of the stem. But -Labe seems to draw the accent one syllable toward itself.' This is a transcription convention implying penultimate accent as the default in his River/Hill Patwin material, not an analysis; Shafer 1961 claimed tones for Patwin (not obtained).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress; Björklund's data are archival Cortina Hill Patwin recordings (Bright 1952) and Lawyer 2021's weight classes are labelled Hill Patwin; Kroeber's note covers isolated place names and vocabulary from River and Hill Patwin informants.
new_statements.identity_note: Patwin (patw1250) comprises Hill, River and South Patwin dialect groups (Lawyer 2021 ch. 1). The weight-sensitive statement (Björklund 2024 after Lawyer 2021) rests on Cortina Hill Patwin recordings and Lawyer's 'Tentative syllable weight classes in Hill Patwin'; Kroeber 1932's penult-default note covers River (Grimes, Colusa) and Hill Patwin informants. No separate glottocodes verified for the dialects here.
